ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that points A, B, and C are sequentially on the circle $\odot o$. Given that $\angle B - \angle A = 40^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle AOB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, $AC$ intersects $OB$ at point $D$,\\
$\because$ $\angle A + \angle O + \angle ADO = 180^\circ$, $\angle B + \angle C + \angle CDB = 180^\circ$, $\angle ADO = \angle CDB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle A + \angle O = \angle B + \angle C$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B - \angle A = \angle O - \angle C = 40^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\overset{\frown}{AB} = \overset{\frown}{AB}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle O = 2\angle C$,\\
$\therefore$ $2\angle C - \angle C = 40^\circ$,\\
Solving this: $\angle C = 40^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AOB = 2 \times 40^\circ = \boxed{80^\circ}$.
